# Booking confirmation with buttons

This recipe sends a customer a native booking card for their appointment, followed by **Confirm** and **Reschedule** buttons, and updates your booking system when they tap one. It uses `sendInteractive`, which needs a [license](/docs/licensing/pricing) on the sending number.

## Before you start

- A Node.js project with `@open-wa/wa-automate` installed (`npm install @open-wa/wa-automate`) and Node.js 22.21.1 or newer.
- A license key for the sending number, in `WA_LICENSE_KEY`.
- A booking record with an ID, a start and end time, a place, and the customer's phone number.

## Send the card and the buttons

The booking card shows the date, time and place in WhatsApp's own details view, with an add-to-calendar option. Reply buttons can't sit on the booking card itself, so send them as a second message. Put the booking ID in each button's `id`; it comes back when the customer taps, so you don't need to track message IDs.

```ts title="bookings.mts"
import { create } from '@open-wa/wa-automate';

const client = await create({ sessionId: 'bookings', licenseKey: process.env.WA_LICENSE_KEY });

type Booking = {
  id: string; phone: string; service: string;
  startAt: string; endAt: string; location: string; manageUrl: string;
};

export async function sendConfirmation(booking: Booking) {
  const to = `${booking.phone}@c.us`;

  await client.sendInteractive(to, {
    type: 'booking',
    title: booking.service,
    body: 'Here are your appointment details.',
    booking: {
      startAt: booking.startAt, // for example '2026-12-03T10:00:00+00:00'
      endAt: booking.endAt,
      location: booking.location,
      managementUrl: booking.manageUrl,
    },
  });

  await client.sendInteractive(to, {
    type: 'buttons',
    body: 'Can you make it?',
    actions: [
      { type: 'reply', id: `confirm:${booking.id}`, label: 'Confirm' },
      { type: 'reply', id: `reschedule:${booking.id}`, label: 'Reschedule' },
    ],
  });
}
```

`sendInteractive` validates the document before sending. A booking needs a `location`, `url` or `phoneNumber`, and `endAt` must be after `startAt`; times with an offset are normalised for you. Each call returns the sent message's ID, which confirms the send, not that the customer saw it.

## Handle the tap

Register the handler once, when your app starts:

```ts title="bookings.mts"
const handled = new Set<string>();

client.onInteractiveResponse(async (response) => {
  if (response.type !== 'reply') return;
  if (handled.has(response.messageId)) return; // the same tap can arrive twice
  handled.add(response.messageId);

  const [action, bookingId] = response.id.split(':');
  if (action === 'confirm') {
    await markConfirmed(bookingId); // your booking system
    await client.sendText(response.chatId, 'Thanks, you are confirmed. See you then.');
  } else if (action === 'reschedule') {
    await client.sendText(response.chatId, `No problem. Pick a new time here: ${await rescheduleLink(bookingId)}`);
  }
});
```

`response.chatId` is the customer's chat, and `response.id` is the button ID you chose. Store `response.messageId` in your database rather than a `Set` if the process can restart, so a repeated delivery doesn't confirm twice.

## From the Easy API

Any language can do the same over HTTP. Send each message to `POST /api/messages/sendInteractive` with `{ "to": "447700900123@c.us", "content": { ... } }`, using the same documents as above:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/messages/sendInteractive \
  -H "X-API-Key: $WA_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"to":"447700900123@c.us","content":{"type":"buttons","body":"Can you make it?","actions":[{"type":"reply","id":"confirm:bk_123","label":"Confirm"},{"type":"reply","id":"reschedule:bk_123","label":"Reschedule"}]}}'
```

Taps arrive as `interactive.response` events, with the response at `payload.response`. Read them from the event stream (`GET /api/events?topics=interactive.response`) or forward them to your backend with a [webhook](/docs/guides/receive-webhooks) by adding `interactive.response` to its `events`.
